card.title: I Predicted This
card.instruction: Create opportunities to show that each impossible event confirms a theory you understood long before anyone asked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I predicted the cupboard would speak. Here: a change in storage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful prediction covers several forms of expression.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cupboard spoke! Fetch my prediction: 'Storage will develop a voice.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need plates, not your notebook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask it politely. I've maintained for years that neglected furniture demands recognition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It wants its name on the dinner invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly: recognition. Put it beside me; I can explain how long I've expected this.

mechanism: A uses the speaking cupboard and its demand for recognition to display a supposedly longstanding furniture theory.
confusable: Unlike defending a vague prediction against a wet-ink accusation, A must use successive impossible developments as fresh confirmation of a prior theory.
comparison: The cupboard alternative turns a social demand into confirmation of neglected-furniture recognition; the pet alternative generalizes an elevation theory through a second animal.
